scope: Thread-routing metric emission for the AI conversation threading slice.

owner.note: The emitter for the thread-routing metric lives with the thread router because that is its only caller in the TypeScript source.

otherParty.note: team2 owns the bot runtime metrics source file and therefore the rest of the metrics surface.

namespace.scaling: selectedScore is scaled by 1000 before rounding; every other value is max(0, round(value))

behaviour.delivery: fire-and-forget; a metric failure must never change the thread routing outcome

ask.action: When porting bot_runtime_metrics.ts to Rust, reuse the thread-routing emitter owned by team1 instead of re-implementing the metrics:bot:threading:* key namespace. Do not create a second writer for these keys.
ask.method: team2 may import crate::utils::ai_threading::thread_router's emitter, or team1 may expose the emitter as a standalone public function; the integration team picks one when applying the central patch.

verification.note: Authoring wave only. Runtime verification requires an integration execution lease. No Cargo, rustfmt, Node, Docker or network command has been run.

integrationDecision.rule: Reuse one concrete emitter; no duplicate namespace writer; no feature acceptance claimed
integrationDecision.signature: Team1 to publish stable Rust signature/types with ready handoff

items: pub struct ThreadRoutingMetric { pub channel_id: String, pub created: bool, pub reused: bool, pub failed: bool, pub candidate_count: i64, pub selected_score: f64, pub prompt_turns_used: i64, pub user_evictions: i64, pub channel_evictions: i64, pub latency_ms: i64 }
pub async fn record_thread_routing_metric(conn: &mut redis::aio::ConnectionManager, prefix: &str, m: &ThreadRoutingMetric) -> Result<(), ThreadStoreError>

behaviour.ttl: all three keys expire with SEMANTIC_METRICS_TTL_SECONDS (86_400). The source uses SEMANTIC_METRICS_TTL_SECONDS for the metric keys and THREAD_TTL_SECONDS for the thread keys; the two are deliberately NOT coupled even though the numbers coincide today.
behaviour.delivery: fire-and-forget. The router calls record_metric, which clones the connection and spawns a task that discards the result (let _ = ...). A metric failure can never fail the routing call.
behaviour.keyPrefix: passed in per call; the router holds DEFAULT_METRICS_PREFIX unless a constructor argument overrides it. No module-scope environment read.

publishedApi.consumerRule: The observability team (owner of src/utils/observability/bot_runtime_metrics.ts) MUST call this emitter rather than write the metrics:bot:threading:* keys itself. Single writer.
